summary: Tested the new Forgot Password / Reset Password feature end-to-end (backend + frontend). Backend: created /app/backend/tests/test_password_reset.py (7 pytest cases) - all PASS: unknown email -> generic 200 with NO reset_url, registered normal user -> generic 200 with NO reset_url (no link leak), bogus token -> 400 'invalid or already used', token<10 chars / password<8 chars -> 422, and full owner bootstrap E2E (forgot-password returns reset_url for sun@sohighon.ai -> reset-password 200 -> token reuse 400 -> login with new password 200 -> /api/auth/me is_admin=true, no _id leak). Frontend (Playwright, preview URL): (1) Login modal shows auth-forgot-link in Log in mode; clicking it renders auth-forgot-view with auth-forgot-email/auth-forgot-submit/auth-forgot-back; 'Back to log in' returns to the login form; empty email shows auth-error 'Enter your email'. (2) Registered qapw47305@example.com via signup (redirected to /portal), logged out, submitted forgot-password -> auth-forgot-sent shown ('If an account exists for ... a reset link is on its way') and auth-forgot-owner-link count=0 (correctly no link for non-owner). (3) Owner E2E via reset page: browser fetch to /api/auth/forgot-password for sun@sohighon.ai returned reset_url; navigating to it rendered reset-password-page + both inputs; mismatched passwords showed reset-error "Passwords don't match."; valid submit showed reset-done and auto-redirected to '/'; logging in with the NEW password succeeded, redirected to /portal, and /account shows owner-tools (Admin tools - super-owner access) panel. (4) /reset-password with no token shows reset-no-token 'Invalid reset link'; an invalid/expired token surfaces the backend message in reset-error. (5) Also verified the owner email in the forgot modal renders auth-forgot-owner-link ('Set a new password now'). Regression: modal login + signup work, logged-in users bounce from / to /portal.

minor.issue: ForgotInput.email is a plain str (not EmailStr), so a malformed value like 'not-an-email' returns 200 generic instead of 422. Harmless (no enumeration, no email sent) but input validation is weaker than other endpoints.

No rate limiting on this endpoint - it can be hammered for an existing account, and each call deletes the previous token (delete_many), so an attacker could repeatedly invalidate a legitimate user's in-flight reset link. Consider a per-email/IP throttle.

issues: Footer copy 'Payments are processed securely by Razorpay.' is still rendered in the password-reset view where it is irrelevant/confusing. Consider hiding it when mode === 'forgot'.

The <8 char password case never reaches the JS reset-error branch because the input has native minLength=8, so the user only sees the browser's default validation bubble instead of the styled reset-error message. Functionally fine, inconsistent with the mismatch error UX.
Coupon expiry uses the browser's native date input (mm/dd/yyyy) instead of the shadcn calendar component used elsewhere.
Console shows 401 'Failed to load resource' from the session/me probe on every anonymous page load - cosmetic noise.

action_items: CLEANUP (as planned by main agent): sun@sohighon.ai now has password 'OwnerFresh456' and there is ONE unused live token in db.password_resets for that email (created by the last modal test). Delete the owner account + password_resets docs before handing back to the real user.
Optional: use EmailStr for ForgotInput.email and add throttling to /api/auth/forgot-password.

critical_code_review_comments: reset_password() correctly hashes with bcrypt, marks the token single-use, clears user_sessions and login_attempts - verified via API (reuse -> 400, old password no longer valid).

The owner-bootstrap branch is properly gated by is_owner_email(email) AND not _email_configured(); confirmed a normal registered user receives no reset_url. Once RESEND_API_KEY is set this path disappears automatically - good.

AuthModal.jsx and ResetPassword.jsx build the API base from window.location.origin instead of process.env.REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL. It works behind this ingress but deviates from the project convention used elsewhere and will break if the app is ever served from a different origin than the API.
